- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts show gradual upward drift, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70.00), model tends to overshoot; cap forecast growth to +1.5–2.0% per day post-spike.  
- If official supply net is negative and sentiment is bearish, model underestimates downside risk — adjust downward by 0.5–1.0% per event.  
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price history shows mean reversion, model often overfits recent trends — apply smoothing filter to reduce momentum bias.  
- For 30-day forecasts with high event count (≥18 events), model tends to overreact to recent auctions — dampen forecast by 0.3–0.7% per event beyond 15.  
- If sentiment is bearish and price is trending up, model often fails to recognize reversal — add early warning buffer (e.g., 1–2% downward adjustment if sentiment drops below 0.33).
